headline: Downtown housing zoning change gets push for faster review; $30,000 and $20,000 grant transfers approved.
summary: JHM Group gave an update on the Riverside Avenue project, and Carrier reviewed its downtown work, including plans for 15 and 24 apartments. The city took over the Chippany golf course, and it is seeking a management company.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, including the communications item and the economic development grants and marketing report.
Approved a letter supporting a downtown zoning change for housing and asking for a faster public hearing.
Approved transferring $30,000 from economic development expenses to the facade improvement grant program account.
Approved transferring $20,000 from economic development expenses to the small business grant program account.
Approved a 2027 meeting calendar with no August meeting.
discussion: Downtown zoning change timing: Members said the amendment should not be delayed by other city work, and they discussed sending a letter to keep it on schedule.

Riverside Avenue project: Members asked about the unit count and why the parking ratio dropped. JHM Group said the unit count still depends on historic preservation review, and zoning changes shaped the parking plan.
Carrier downtown projects: Members asked about the Middle Street property and whether it could include housing. Staff said it would be commercial and industrial.
Chippany golf course: Members asked about fees and staff presence at the course. November introductory rates are $40 for 18 holes and $20 for nine holes, and spring rates will differ.
Forestville factory buildings: Members discussed a master plan that would speed tenant approvals in large buildings. Staff said each new tenant now needs a special permit and site plan.
